Package common.utility.dashboard

Class Dashboard

java.lang.Object
common.utility.dashboard.Dashboard
public class Dashboard extends Object
Puts robot values, buttons and the auto picker on the dashboard, in one line each. 

 Dashboard.add("voltage", RobotController::getBatteryVoltage);
 Supplier<Command> auto = Dashboard.addAutoChooser("Auto", "Default Auto", autos);

Values with a supplier are updated every loop, on the robot's own thread. Use a / in a name to group values, e.g. "Tests/Intake". Adding a name again replaces the old one.

Everything goes to two dashboards for now:

  • Elastic, through SmartDashboard's NetworkTables entries, under the full name.
  • NarwhalDashboard, under the part of the name after the last /, which is the key its web page looks for.
This is the only class that knows how values reach a dashboard: retiring NarwhalDashboard (see its class comment for the plan), or moving off SmartDashboard when WPILib removes it in 2027, should only change this class.

      public static Supplier<edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Command> addAutoChooser(String name, String defaultAuto, Map<String,edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Command> autos)
      Shows a dropdown for picking the auto. On NarwhalDashboard it's the auto picker; an auto picked there wins over the one picked on Elastic.
      Parameters:
      name - Name of the dropdown on the dashboard
      defaultAuto - Name of the auto that runs if no one picks one
      autos - Each auto, by the name shown in the dropdown, in the order to show them
